body:
# id(world_fixture): `decode` accepts duplicate JSON fields in header and event lines — `check_keys` and the window check only ever see the collapsed last value

## Summary

`world_fixture::decode` (`pkgs/id/src/world_fixture.rs:558`) is documented as "Parse a fixture, refusing anything it cannot replay faithfully", and its field discipline is strict on purpose: `check_keys` (`:1284`) requires **exactly** the expected fields per line — no unknown ones, none missing — and `check_window` (`:1350`) requires sequenced events to be contiguous and within the header's sequence. But both the header (`decode_header`, `:1106`) and every event line (`decode_event`, `:1195`) are first parsed with `serde_json::from_str::<Value>` (`:1108`, `:1199`), and serde_json's `Value` object is last-wins for duplicate keys. By the time `check_keys` runs, a duplicated field has already collapsed to one — so a line that names the same field twice with **different** values is accepted, and the value that survives is whichever came last:

| # | Line shape | Result today | What should happen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | header with `"world":"first","world":"second"` | `Ok`, `world_id = "second"` | an ambiguous header is refused — the fixture names two worlds |
| 2 | header with `"fixture":99,"fixture":1` | `Ok` (version check sees 1) | the version gate (`:1124`) must see the duplication, not just the surviving value: as written, an unsupported version is hidden in plain sight |
| 3 | chat event with `"sequence":99,"sequence":1` under a header at sequence 1 (complete) | `Ok` | the window check (`check_window`) validates the collapsed sequence; the raw line claimed an out-of-window sequence first and is not a faithful record of any session |
| 4 | header `records` object with a repeated record key | collapsed once by the `Value` parse, then re-serialized (`:1170`) and collapsed **again** inside `parse_records` | refused at the first parse (see companion issue for the `parse_records` side) |

This is the same silent-discard class as #6390 (atlas-eval duplicate results key) and #6384 (deploy.py duplicate registry keys): in a format whose whole purpose is faithful replay (`verify` replays a fixture twice and compares records after every event), an ambiguous line must be a parse error, not a coin the parser flips silently.

## Evidence

Verified this run on the laptop at origin/main `252d430853` with a probe integration test against the real `id` crate (`~/git/fleet/probe-records-dup/pkgs/id/tests/probe_fixture_dup.rs`, worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-records-dup` @252d430853):

- Control: minimal valid fixture (header, `current_sequence` 0, complete, no events) decodes, `world_id = "w"`.
- Case 1: duplicate `world` → `Ok`, `world_id = "second"`.
- Case 2: duplicate `fixture` version (99 then 1) → `Ok`.
- Case 3: duplicate event `sequence` (99 then 1) → `Ok`; the window check passes on the surviving value.

Probe result: 1 passed (all three bug cases reproduce; control behaves).

Code read @252d430853: `decode_header` at `world_fixture.rs:1106` parses `serde_json::from_str(line)` into a `Value`, then `check_keys` over the collapsed map (`:1132`); `decode_event` at `:1195` does the same per event line (`:1199`, `check_keys` at `:1209`/`:1225`/`:1243`/`:1263`); scalar fields are then read with `u64_field`/`string_field`/`bool_field` from the collapsed map. No duplicate detection in either function. The in-tree tests exercise `check_keys` for unknown/missing fields, which duplicates structurally evade.

## Why it matters

Fixtures are the determinism oracle for world programs: `verify`'s verdict is only meaningful if the fixture text denotes exactly one session. A fixture format that silently resolves contradictory fields lets a hand-edited or corrupted fixture (the exact inputs `decode`'s strictness exists to catch — unknown fields, gaps, blank lines are all refused) replay as a different session than the one its text first describes, and lets the version gate be satisfied by a line that also declares an unsupported version. Every other strictness rule in this decoder is defeated the same way if the field it checks can be duplicated.

## Acceptance criteria

- `decode` refuses any header or event line whose JSON object contains a duplicate field, with an error naming the line and the repeated field (line context follows the existing "fixture line {n}" convention).
- All three shapes above are refused; the version, world, and sequence checks operate on a document known to name each field at most once.
- Valid fixtures are unchanged: the existing `world_fixture` tests (encode/decode round-trips of every kind, window checks, key checks) still pass, and `encode` output always decodes.
- New tests pin duplicate-field refusal for the header and for at least one event kind.
- The header `records` field: a repeated record key inside it is refused here as a duplicate field of the records object (not merely by whatever `parse_records` does after re-serialization) — coordinate with the companion `parse_records` issue so the two fixes agree on where nested duplicates are caught.
